rationale: bugs_open/215's quiet-mode mechanism (register PLAN-048, live v1.0.1288) makes both canonicalisation surfaces honour a page's STORED identity instead of re-deriving it, but only for a plan page the reconciler marked identity_authority='realised'. The marker is minted in exactly two functions: snapPlanPageOntoRealised (Pass B url-exact + the three twin layers) and normaliseRealisedToPlanPage (Pass A's union). NO ROUTE COVERED THE COMMONEST SHAPE OF ALL: a plan entry that names a realised page EXACTLY as it is stored. Pass B2 pairs those entries and mutates only lm['sections']; matchTwinIdentity runs before it and its shared 'eligible' closure refuses a same-name candidate; the path_key layer is skipped because validate-shaped plan entries carry no url. So realisedIdentityOf returns ok=false, neither honour branch fires, CanonicalisePage re-derives the page at its role's default hub, and the (site_id,name) upsert misses and INSERTs a second row. For a stored name that is not a fixed point of the canonicaliser this was UNREACHABLE BY CONFIGURATION. Proven live, not argued: loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk measured the population (38 of 45 pages not fixed points, 17 by name), seeded honour_realised_identity, fired one re-plan on 2026-08-17, and 19 phantom pages were INSERTed anyway - 17 the predicted tool-<name> twins (corr 6fe6ee93-67b9-4831-bf17-2ca473e1d30c, chassis v1.0.1305, reconcile_result.pages_restamped: 0). That lane's D6 planner work is blocked on this fix. THE FIX stamps the stored identity at the head of Pass B2. It is NOT routed through the existing snap arm on purpose: a snap replaces the whole entry from the realised row, and Pass B2's standing contract is that only 'sections' is touched (title/meta/nav stay the LLM's), which is how a re-plan refreshes copy; snapping would discard that for every correctly-named page and, flag-off, file a warning per page per re-plan (~17 on LMC, ~31 on webdesign.co.uk), reporting the good case as damage. THIS IS NOT NEW AUTHORITY, and that is the claim to attack hardest. No new config key: the change widens the population the EXISTING honour_realised_identity opt-in already covers, whose documented contract is 'keep that page's STORED name/url/page_type' - a page the planner named verbatim is the paradigm case of it. The structure aspect stays at five opt-in keys, so RFC_022's N=10 action-surface budget is untouched. No writer edits (so TestIdentityPolicyReachesBothCanonicalisationSurfaces needs no re-anchoring, checked not assumed), no new DB reads. The stamp is UNGATED, exactly like Pass B's snap and Pass A's union, because the reconciler decides identity and the writers decide whether to honour it - and that division is only safe if every stamped field is inert to a non-honouring writer: identity_authority has no reader outside realisedIdentityOf (both call sites inside if identityPolicy.HonourRealisedIdentity); url is derived and overwritten by both surfaces when not honouring; page_type is NOT inert (it feeds Role, hence CanonicalisePage), which is why the type-equality precondition exists - we only ever write back the value the writer would have derived anyway. parent_section and slug are deliberately NOT stamped: both feed the writers' canonicalisation, so writing them would change flag-OFF behaviour and the inertness argument with it. CONSUMERS TOLD, per the 2026-07-29 ruling 3: three sites carry honour_realised_identity today [MEASURED 2026-08-19] - fundamentallyai.com (+twin_identity_snap), loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk, loancalculator.co.uk. Their next re-plan changes behaviour, and it is exactly what they opted in FOR; the other five current structure specs carry no identity key and are byte-unaffected. ONE CANDIDATE REMEDY IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, which is why the fix is not where the bug file suggested. The 08-19 addendum proposed 'drop rname == lname from the canonical layer's eligibility'. That edit is INERT: 'eligible' holds two refusals in series and the second subsumes the first (a candidate whose name equals the plan entry's name is necessarily a name the plan carries, so planNames[rname] always fires too). Mutation-proved three ways - removing either clause alone leaves every test green, removing both turns TestReconcile_TwinLayersRefuseTheEntryItself red. Anyone taking that remedy would have shipped a no-op and been unable to tell it from an empty population. The second candidate (write path treats a name match as realised-derived) is declined on architecture: it gives both write surfaces their own pages knowledge and a second seam deciding identity, against this lane's established division, and would let any LLM page named like a realised row seize that identity without the preservation set, forgery strip or refusals. OBSERVABILITY, designed against a zero this lane already read backwards. PLAN-048's old verify-later predicted the dark-launch counters would move off zero on the first re-plan; [MEASURED 2026-08-19] they are zero fleet-wide all time against a live instrument, and NOT for want of demand - the 08-17 re-plan minted 19 phantoms while all three codes stayed at zero, because a same-name page is refused by 'eligible' BEFORE any layer records an observation. The commonest shape was invisible to the instrument built to measure it. So the new signal is one summary row per run - PLAN_PAGE_SAME_NAME_IDENTITY_HELD (info, flag on) or PLAN_PAGE_SAME_NAME_TWIN_PENDING (warning, flag off) - carrying every (plan_name, stored_url, would_derive_name) triple, plus PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_TYPE_CONFLICT per refused pair. Only DIVERGING stamps are recorded (a fixed-point stamp prevented nothing); per-page rows were rejected as noise. The codes' own remedy text states the mandatory join: classify each would_derive_name against pages before quoting a count, or a twin about to be minted is conflated with one already there. BLD-018's parked reuse question (siteUsesFlatURLs + siteIdentityPolicyFor are two typed readers of one site_specs row, 'consolidation is theirs to absorb when they next touch it') was CONSIDERED and is DEFERRED, stated rather than skipped: the only edit here to site_identity_policy.go is documentation, and attaching a DB-read-topology refactor of two live write surfaces to a fix whose entire safety story is flag-off inertness is the shared-seam-smuggled-inside-a-bug-patch shape the 2026-07-28 ruling forbids. Recorded in PLAN-048 so it is not silent. REGISTERED IN THE SAME COMMIT per the 2026-07-28 ordering exemption's surviving condition: PLAN-048 gains the fourth minting route, the three new codes, the measured redundancy finding, three stated limitations, and its falsified verify-later marked as such with the reason. OUT OF SCOPE, stated: the preservation-set hole (a realised row neither deployed nor needs_rebuild on a site with a current plan never enters realisedByName, so its twin is still mintable - lower severity, the twin of an unbuilt page); role-disagreeing same-name pairs (refused by design, durably recorded); the seven both-deployed twin pairs and which name survives (owner decision per pair, O2's runbook); bugs_open/204/214/266 adjacencies.

edits.rationale: The fix. A new helper that stamps the realised identity onto a plan entry paired with a realised page by EXACT name - the case no marker-minting route covered. Two guards, both mutation-proved. Type equality is compared through firstNonEmptyField(lm,'page_type','type','role'), the writers' OWN Role derivation, not page_type alone: an entry carrying its role under 'role' would otherwise be misread as a conflict and left unprotected. The complete-triple check mirrors realisedIdentityOf's own refusal so the counters can never claim a stamp the reader would reject (a guard that never fires reads exactly like one that is absent). A role disagreement is REFUSED and recorded, never reconciled - honouring it would silently retype a live page. WouldDeriveName is a name-only classification for the durable record and never a gate on the stamp: predicting the writers' full answer would need parent_section and the site's URL shape, which this function deliberately does not read.

Call site, at the HEAD of the Pass B2 block so it covers all three section branches and the fall-through: who owns a page's NAME does not depend on whether its composition was restored, forced empty or left alone. Ungated, like Pass B's snap and Pass A's union - see the rationale's per-field inertness argument.

edits.rationale: The durable record, because an active chassis pod retains under a second of log (bugs_open/136 §11). Split into a PURE builder plus a thin persister so the shape of what gets recorded is unit- and mutation-testable without a database. One summary row per run rather than one per page: the stamp fires on every same-name pairing (~17/re-plan on LMC, ~31 on webdesign.co.uk) and per-page rows would bury the events that mean something. Two codes because the same observation means opposite things either side of the flag. The remedy text carries the mandatory classifying join, so a later reader cannot quote a count without it.

Counters and their two carrier types, plus the ValidateSitePlanAction wiring. The policy read is hoisted out of its if-block ONLY so the recorder can be told which side of the flag the run is on - the same set of pages is a no-op record with the flag on and a list of twins about to be written with it off. reconcileOptions is deliberately NOT widened: the reconciler stamps unconditionally, and only the writers gate.

Records the MEASURED redundancy in the 'eligible' closure, at the closure. Both clauses stay - each states a different intent and neither costs anything - but a reader must know that removing one is behaviour-neutral while removing both is not, or they will repeat the addendum's inert remedy. This is the comment that stops the next session 'simplifying' the guard on the belief that the other clause is the load-bearing one. Also updates the forgery-strip comment and the Pass B2 header, which both enumerated the minting routes and would otherwise now be wrong.

edits.rationale: DOCUMENTATION ONLY, no code change - and it is the edit the LMC lane explicitly asked for. This file presented the three switches as independently gated behaviours and asked (rightly) for the population to be measured before enabling HonourRealisedIdentity. That lane did exactly that, enabled exactly that flag, and got 19 phantoms, because nothing here said the flag cannot fire at all for a page no pass has paired. Now it does: the four minting routes are enumerated with which are gated, the 08-17 incident is cited by correlation, and the surviving preconditions (preservation set, type agreement) are named. realisedIdentityOf's comment records that ok=false is two different answers wearing one face.

edits.rationale: Ten tests, every fixture using the real stored names from the 08-17 incident rather than shapes invented to suit the code. TestReconcile_LMCCanaryShape_NoTwinIsMintable reproduces that run's exact plan shape (names verbatim, no url, sections: [], every layer off) and drives it through the REAL extractPagesFromPlan to the reader the write surfaces use - red without the fix. TestReconcile_TwinLayersRefuseTheEntryItself pins a behaviour nothing pinned before, and its doc comment states exactly what it pins and what it does NOT (see the rationale's refutation). MUTATION EVIDENCE, run not predicted: stamp call removed -> 8 red; stamp gated on a flag -> 7 red; type-equality dropped -> red; complete-triple dropped -> red; url not stamped -> 3 red incl. the step-boundary test; type read from page_type alone -> red; fixed-point stamps reported as diverging -> 2 red; forged url left in place -> red; flag-off record downgraded to the flag-on code -> red. Suites verified on a git archive HEAD shadow tree so another lane's uncommitted work in the same package cannot flatter the result.

Register entry PLAN-048 updated in the SAME commit that ships the seam, per the 2026-07-28 ordering exemption's surviving condition. Four things it did not say and a reader would have been misled by: its status still read 'enabled on no site' (three sites carry the flag); it had no fourth minting route; its guards list omitted the clause that turns out to be redundant; and its verify-later PREDICTED the dark-launch counters would move off zero, which is now falsified - marked as such with the reason, because the way it failed (the counters cannot see a same-name page at all) is the finding. Also records the three stated limitations and the BLD-018 deferral, so neither is silent. Index row refreshed to match.

plan.summary: bugs_open/215: stamp the realised page identity at Pass B2, so honour_realised_identity can finally reach a page the planner names EXACTLY as it is stored - the shape no marker-minting route covered, which left the flag unreachable by configuration and minted 19 phantom pages on a live canary that had opted in. Flag-off byte-inert by construction; no new config key; the reconciler keeps deciding identity and the two write surfaces are unchanged. Register PLAN-048 updated in the same commit.
